models_evaluated: 3D convolutional neural network for SMAO detection

links.outcome: Prospective performance of the model on live CT examinations, including sensitivity, specificity, and QA-confirmed missed findings
links.effect: Prospective sensitivity 67.6% and specificity 99.6% (AUC 0.917), versus 50.0% sensitivity on the test set; 237 cases flagged for QA, 83 (35.0%) confirmed as missed SMAO.
links.quote: Prospectively, sensitivity was 67.6% and specificity was 99.6% (AUC = 0.917).

links.outcome: Findings missed on initial radiologist read and identified by AI QA review
links.effect: Of 237 QA-flagged cases, 83 (35.0%) were confirmed missed SMAO, indicating 40.7% of SMAO cases were undiagnosed on the initial read.
links.quote: The model flagged 237 cases for QA review, of which 83 (35.0%) were confirmed as missed SMAO, indicating that 40.7% of SMAO cases were undiagnosed on the initial read.

unlisted_practices: Using AI to triage/prioritize radiology worklist and reduce reporting delays
Using AI as a retrospective quality assurance tool to identify missed findings
NLP-based identification of positive reports to build training data

screen.reason: The study prospectively deployed a 3D deep learning model to screen 79,163 real-time clinical CT exams, testing a quality assurance and alert workflow for detecting missed superior mesenteric artery occlusions.

primary.practice: real-time quality assurance flagging for missed diagnoses
